sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Fiscal Decentralization**: The collapse of the **Jagirdari system** led to the rise of **Ijaradari (Revenue Farming)**, where rights were auctioned to the highest bidder, causing peasant exploitation.
• **Commercialization of Agriculture**: Shift from subsistence to cash crops (indigo, cotton, opium) driven by European demand and the need for liquid cash to pay revenue.
• **Banking & Finance**: Emergence of powerful **Jagath Seths** and indigenous banking houses (Shroffs) who financed regional states and the EIC.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The 'Drain of Wealth' mechanism began post-1757, shifting India from a net exporter of bullion to a net exporter of raw materials.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Dominance of Zamindars; shift to Ijaradari; high revenue demand.
Need for cash to pay state taxes; monetization of rural economy.
Mains: Impact of land revenue on peasant indebtedness.
Decline of traditional trade routes; rise of coastal port cities (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras).
Prelims: Shift in trade centers from inland to coastal.

items.definition: A system of revenue farming where the state contracted the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder, leading to short-term extraction over long-term agricultural investment.
Indigenous bankers who facilitated credit, currency exchange, and hundi (bill of exchange) operations, essential for the 18th-century credit market.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Hundi System**: A sophisticated indigenous credit instrument used for long-distance trade, functioning like a modern bill of exchange.
• **Monetization**: Increased use of silver rupees as the standard medium of exchange across regional kingdoms.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Political instability (Maratha-Mughal conflicts), lack of centralized currency, and predatory taxation.
• **Solutions**: Emergence of regional stability in Bengal and Mysore which briefly fostered proto-industrialization.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'I-C-A-N' (18th Century Economy).
• **Decoded Meaning**: I-Ijaradari, C-Commercialization, A-Agrarian distress, N-New banking (Shroffs).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not assume the 18th century was a period of total economic stagnation. Recent historiography (e.g., C.A. Bayly) highlights 'regional prosperity' and 'proto-industrialization' in areas like Bengal and Mysore.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Commercialization of Agriculture' to explain the transition from a subsistence-based medieval economy to a colonial-linked market economy.

keyTakeaways: The 18th century was a period of transition, not just decline.
Ijaradari system replaced the stable Mughal revenue administration.
Indigenous banking (Shroffs/Hundis) remained the backbone of trade until the mid-19th century.
